churn_resistance.rationale: Boundaries are excellent: all API I/O, types and caching live in lib/api.ts, derived data in lib/data.ts, formatting in lib/format.ts, config in one file, and no reliance on framework internals — an upgrade touches few files. What keeps it off 5 is that the manual cache in lib/api.ts re-implements what the framework now ships, and the absence of Suspense boundaries means the documented migration to Cache Components will flag all seven routes.

findings.issue: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' is the previous-generation caching model. Next 16.4 (the current stable) recommends Cache Components for every app, and with cacheComponents enabled this export is a build error; it becomes the default in Next 17.
findings.suggestion: Enable cacheComponents in next.config.ts and delete the export — uncached data already runs at request time under the new model (see nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components, section 'dynamic = "force-dynamic"').

findings.issue: A hand-rolled 60s TTL Map with LRU-ish trimming duplicates the framework's data caching ('use cache' + cacheLife('minutes')), which the migration guide notes also defaults to in-memory storage — the same semantics, maintained by the framework instead of by this file.
findings.suggestion: Convert get() into a 'use cache' function with cacheLife('minutes') once cacheComponents is on; keep the NotFoundError/find/list surface so pages don't change.

findings.issue: fetch() has no timeout or AbortController, so a slow upstream API blocks the server render indefinitely with no fallback path.
findings.suggestion: Use AbortSignal.timeout() (Node 24 supports it) and map the abort to the error boundary, or wrap data-heavy sections in Suspense so the shell still streams.

findings.location: app/app/ (no loading.tsx or <Suspense> in any route)
findings.issue: No streaming boundaries anywhere; under Cache Components' instant-navigation validation every route will report an insight and need Suspense added after the fact.
findings.suggestion: Add loading.tsx (or Suspense around the heavy sections like moves/evolution) now, so the app already has the structure the current model validates for.

findings.issue: Raw with an eslint-disable for @next/next/no-img-element instead of the framework's Image component; each usage needs a suppression comment, so the workaround is copy-pasted.
findings.suggestion: Either configure images.remotePatterns for the API origin and use next/image, or centralize the decision in one <Sprite> component so the suppression (and the reasoning) exists in exactly one place.

findings.issue: slug() strips diacritics with a regex containing raw combining characters ([̀-ͯ]) — invisible in review and easy to corrupt; the range is also narrower than Unicode diacritics.
findings.suggestion: Use text.normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{Diacritic}/gu, '') (Unicode property escapes, supported by the ES2023 target).

findings.issue: idFromUrl parses API URLs with a hand-rolled regex rather than the URL parser the platform provides.
findings.suggestion: Use new URL(url).pathname and match the trailing segment, which is self-documenting and can't silently mis-parse on a URL shape change.

findings.issue: prefetch={false} on every card and pagination link forfeits instant navigations; under the current model's partial prefetching, cached UI is prefetched by default for exactly this card-grid case.
findings.suggestion: Once data is cached with 'use cache', drop prefetch={false} on cards so prefetching serves the cached UI; keep it only where prefetching would be genuinely wasteful.

findings.issue: Inline <title> inside the error component relies on React hoisting rather than the metadata API (which error.tsx cannot export) — a valid workaround but an undocumented-looking one.
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but add a one-line comment (like the one in lib/api.ts) noting why the metadata route isn't available here, so a future reader doesn't 'fix' it.

findings.issue: @types/node is pinned to ^20 while the runtime is Node 24.
findings.suggestion: Bump to ^24 so types match the runtime's APIs (e.g. AbortSignal.timeout, structuredClone).

summary: This is a lean, well-factored app pinned to the newest stable Next.js with genuinely excellent boundaries — every fetch, type and cache decision lives in lib/api.ts, so a framework change is contained. Its one real forward-looking debt is that the data-loading model (force-dynamic + no-store + a hand-rolled in-memory TTL cache) is the previous generation: the current stable release already recommends Cache Components, makes it the create-next-app default, and will make it the default in Next 17, where the layout's route-segment config becomes a build error. Migration would touch only three places (one config line, lib/api.ts, and adding Suspense boundaries), which is exactly why the structure earns trust despite the model lag.
